sources: https://www.ksoutdoors.gov/about-kdwp/where-we-work/state-parks/cedar-bluff (read in a browser 2026-11-06): 'The Page Creek Area, on the south shore of the reservoir ... provides some of the finest primitive camping in the state with its large shade trees and sandy shorelines. The Page Creek Area contains 36 utility campsites, a community shelter, two dumpstations, two boatramp facilities, two showerhouses and two vault toilets; one designated primitive campground and numerous undesignated campsites'; Areas table: Page Creek 'Reservable Sites: No', 'Primitive Camping: 243', 'Water, Electric: 37'; office (785) 726-3212.

https://www.campitks.gov/camping/cedar-bluff-state-park/r/campgroundDetails.page?parkID=519115, read 2026-11-06: 'Open year round.'; Directions: 'The Page Creek Area is located 19 miles south of I-70's 135 exit on highway 147, and 3 miles west on Trego County Road CC'; 2027 holiday 3-night minimums and the 14-consecutive-night rule (bulletins).

campitks.gov campsiteDetails.page for every Page Creek site, read 2026-11-06: Pronghorn 401-420 ('Camphost is located in Site 407. 401-406 & 408-410 are Seasonal Campsites (available at monthly rate). Sites 411-420 are reservable. All sites contain water and 50 AMP electrical service. All concrete pads'; 407 typed full hookup; 100-110 ft back-ins; 'Proximity to Water: Within 1 Mile'); Prickly Pear 451-467 ('Campground consists of 17, two utility (water and electricty) campsites. Camping pads are surfaced with asphalt'; 451 'reserved for the Page Creek Area camp host'; 13 at 30/20 A, 4 at 50 A; 463-467 pull-through 150-200 ft; 'Within 1/4 Mile'); designated primitive loops Crooked Arrow (16), Muley (4) and Whitetail (9) on the shore; 'River/Lake View: Y' on every site.

Esri World Imagery with the per-site coordinates (38.7760,-99.7700 at 1300 m), 2026-11-06: Pronghorn (centroid 38.7755,-99.7649) sits ~300 m back from the east-arm shore, where the Crooked Arrow primitive sites are; Prickly Pear (38.7778,-99.7783) is ~100-150 m from the nearest bay behind trees, ~1.2 km west of Pronghorn on its own spur road. Stored pin (38.7723,-99.7594) is on the Muley primitive point, ~590 m SE of Pronghorn and 1.7 km from Prickly Pear.

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule)

values.note: Page Creek's sites are listed on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov); Pronghorn 411-420 are named as reservable, while 401-406 and 408-410 are monthly seasonal sites and 407 and Prickly Pear 451 are camp-host sites. KDWP's own park page still says 'Reservable Sites: No' for Page Creek. 2027 holiday minimum 3 nights; up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground.

note: Quieter south-shore area of Cedar Bluff Reservoir: two utility loops (Pronghorn, 50 A concrete pads; Prickly Pear, asphalt pads about 1.2 km west), shoreline primitive loops and wide undesignated primitive camping, two showerhouses, two dump stations, two boat ramps. --Claude
summary: Confirmed showers, dump, reservable (Pronghorn 411-420 named reservable on the booking site). Added 50 A + water (no public sewer), 37 utility sites to 200 ft with pull-throughs, vault toilets, 2027 holiday 3-night minimum, 14-night rule, open year round. Fees left as recorded (AWH 2026-10-15). Lakeview confirmed (all sites 'Within 1/4 Mile' or '1 Mile' + lake view; utility loops 100-300 m back). Pin ~590 m off; split candidate.
flags: Pin move: stored 38.7723,-99.7594 is on the Muley primitive point, ~590 m SE of the Pronghorn utility loop. Suggest 38.7755,-99.7649 (Pronghorn centroid, the reservable loop).

Split candidate: Prickly Pear (17 W/E sites, centroid 38.7778,-99.7783) is ~1.2 km west of Pronghorn (38.7755,-99.7649) on its own spur road off the Page Creek road. Both are Page Creek loops and share the area's showerhouses (Prickly Pear is 'near the Apache Showerhouse').

Reservability conflict: KDWP's park page says Page Creek 'Reservable Sites: No'; the booking site lists every Page Creek site site-specific and says 'Sites 411-420 are reservable'. Recorded reservable true from the booking site. The stored note's 'Reservable online Apr 1-Sep 30; FCFS Oct-Mar' could not be confirmed and is dropped.
Long-stay share (state park, informational): 9 of Pronghorn's 20 sites are monthly seasonal, 2 sites are camp hosts; 25 of 37 utility sites sold nightly or FCFS.

Sand: KDWP describes Page Creek's 'sandy shorelines' with undesignated primitive camping; the developed utility loops are on concrete/asphalt pads, so this is a developed loop that also offers beach-side primitive camping - stays.
